bodyHtml:
Where company training fits in Canada's certification system

Canada certifies most NDT technicians centrally. The CGSB scheme, run by the NDT Certification Body at Natural Resources Canada under CAN/CGSB-48.9712, which is based on ISO 9712, means technicians sit exams set by a third party rather than by their employer. That's different from the US employer-based model, and it changes what your company's training is for.

A Canadian NDT company still carries a lot of training responsibility. New hires need grounding before they sit anything. Certified technicians need to learn your procedures, your clients' specifications and your reporting standards. Radiography crews need company radiation safety instruction. Client sites in the oil sands or at nuclear stations add their own orientation requirements. And plenty of Canadian companies also hold ASNT SNT-TC-1A written practices for US client work, cross-border projects or sectors where employer-based certification is expected.

The eLearning app in Atlantis NDT ERP is built for that internal training. It is not a route to CGSB certification, and Atlantis doesn't present it as one. Atlantis's own training courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. What the portal does is give your company one place to deliver and record the training that sits around certification: onboarding, procedures, client requirements, safety and refreshers.

Because the portal lives inside the ERP, those records sit next to each technician's certificates, availability and job history, which is where your QA manager and your clients' auditors expect to find them.

What the eLearning app includes

As configured by Atlantis for NDT companies, the portal includes:

  • Level I, II and III sections, so material is grouped by the level a learner works at.
  • Video lessons streamed from OneDrive or SharePoint with download protection, so your videos stay in your Microsoft 365 storage.
  • Quizzes, with questions importable from Word files.
  • Certificates of completion for finished courses.
  • Learner accounts created by admins, with access granted and revoked by admins.
  • A learner dashboard for each person's courses and progress.
  • Auto-join for invited members.
  • Online course sales, if you train outside candidates.
  • A Practical NDT section opening Atlantis's 3D practice platform.

Where you need something beyond this list, such as a particular reporting view for a client audit, it is handled as configuration during implementation and agreed with you up front. No surprises about what's built in and what isn't.

Practical NDT for camps, rotations and long winters

A lot of Canadian NDT work happens far from a training room. Crews fly in and out of oil sands sites north of Fort McMurray, work long rotations at upgraders and plants, or travel between pipeline spreads in remote country. Hands-on practice on real equipment is hard to schedule when the equipment and the Level III are both hundreds of kilometres away.

Practical NDT is Atlantis's immersive 3D, game-like NDT practice platform. Learners work through UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET and TOFD scenarios on virtual welds, pipes, pressure vessels and castings. They set up, scan, find indications and decide what they mean, on a laptop in a camp room if that's where they are.

Every learner enrolled in the eLearning portal gets a Practical NDT section. Access is switched on automatically at enrolment, or an admin can grant it manually.

Canadian companies tend to use it in three ways:

  • Between rotations. Technicians keep a method fresh during time off-site without needing access to your shop.
  • Before exams. Trainees build familiarity with scanning and interpretation before practical sessions on real specimens. Practice on a platform doesn't count as the documented experience a certification scheme requires; it simply prepares people to make better use of real time.
  • Cross-training. UT technicians exploring PAUT and TOFD, or MT technicians moving into ET, get a feel for setups before formal training.

Book a demo of Practical NDT inside eLearning to see a learner's view.

Radiography crews: CNSC and moving sources

Industrial radiography in Canada is licensed by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. People who operate exposure devices must be CNSC-certified exposure device operators, and trainees work under direct supervision while they gain experience. Your company's licence comes with a radiation protection programme, and your radiation safety officer is responsible for training people in the licensee's procedures and keeping records the CNSC can inspect.

Moving sources adds another layer. Transport of Dangerous Goods rules require that people handling or transporting Class 7 radioactive material are trained and hold a training certificate from their employer, with periodic retraining.

The eLearning portal doesn't replace EDO certification, your licence or TDG compliance. It gives your RSO a practical way to deliver company-specific content and prove who completed it. Typical courses:

  • Your operating and emergency procedures, recorded as short video lessons with a quiz.
  • Radiation safety awareness for assistants, helpers and non-radiography staff who work near controlled areas.
  • Refresher content your RSO assigns on a schedule, with completion per person.
  • Source transport briefings for vehicle crews, alongside the Fleet app's record of which vehicles can carry radioactive sources and their transport licence expiry.

The Certificates app's employee NDT profile holds radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry. Practical NDT's RT scenarios let trainees practise technique selection and image interpretation without anyone receiving a dose.

Alberta oil sands, upgraders and ABSA-regulated work

Alberta is the centre of Canadian NDT demand: oil sands mining and in-situ operations, upgraders, refineries and petrochemical plants around Edmonton's Industrial Heartland, and the pipelines that connect them. Pressure equipment in the province falls under ABSA, the pressure equipment safety authority, and owners run inspection programmes under their ABSA-accepted quality management systems. Fabrication follows CSA B51 alongside ASME codes, structural work often references CSA W59, and pipelines are built and maintained to CSA Z662.

For an NDT company, each of those clients and codes brings specific expectations: which procedures apply, what acceptance criteria look like, how reports are laid out and what site orientations technicians must complete. That's the training that fills a Canadian Level III's week, and it's a strong fit for the portal.

  • Client procedure courses. A short course per major client or contract, covering their procedures and your approved techniques, with a quiz written by your Level III.
  • Code awareness courses. Introductions to the relevant sections of CSA Z662 or CSA W59 for technicians moving between pipeline and structural work. Your Level III decides the content; the portal delivers it.
  • Turnaround onboarding. Spring and fall shutdowns bring extra hands. Invite the whole crew to the onboarding course, and auto-join enrols them as they accept.

When the turnaround ends, admins revoke access for temporary staff, so your course library doesn't travel with them.

Ontario nuclear and specialised inspection

Ontario's nuclear sector is a different world. Refurbishment programmes at Darlington and Bruce, and routine outages across the fleet, involve demanding inspection work, much of it eddy current and ultrasonic testing of components under CSA N285.4 periodic inspection requirements. Nuclear operators impose extensive site training, security screening and procedure qualification on every contractor, and they expect records to be exact.

Most of that site-specific training is delivered by the operator. But the NDT company still has to prepare its people: company procedures for nuclear work, quality expectations, human performance tools, reporting discipline and the method knowledge behind specialised techniques.

The portal gives you a structured place for that preparation, with a clear record of who completed what before mobilisation. Practical NDT's ET and UT scenarios offer early familiarity with the methods, though qualification for nuclear inspection is always done on the operator's terms, on real equipment and mock-ups.

Nuclear work also rewards clean access control. Admins create every learner account and grant or revoke access, which keeps sensitive procedure material limited to the people who should see it.

English, French and personal data

Canadian NDT companies often run crews in both official languages, especially those working in Quebec or with crews from Quebec working in Alberta. The portal doesn't translate content automatically, but it handles bilingual training simply: build a French version of a course alongside the English one and invite each technician to the right version. Quiz questions imported from Word work the same way in either language.

Technician training records are personal information. Federal privacy law under PIPEDA, and provincial laws in Alberta, British Columbia and Quebec, shape how you collect and keep that information. The eLearning app gives you practical controls: admin-created accounts, admin-controlled access, and revocation when a person leaves. Decisions about hosting, retention and who in your company can see what are made with you during implementation. Atlantis does not claim the software makes you compliant with any privacy law; your policies do that, and the configuration supports them.

Connecting training to certificates and dispatch

The eLearning app earns its place when it's joined to the rest of Atlantis NDT ERP.

  • Certificates records each technician's certifications, including CGSB (ISO 9712), SNT-TC-1A and others, with level, method, certifying body, issue and expiry dates, OJT and training hours, and vision tests. Certificates expiring within 90 days are flagged with warning tasks, which is your prompt to assign refresher training.
  • Team Assignments uses an availability calendar with a training status, so nobody dispatches a technician to a site in Fort McMurray on the day they're booked for a course.
  • Timesheets warn when a technician's certificate isn't valid.
  • Surveys handle competency questionnaires and course feedback.

How course completions relate to training hours on a technician's record is agreed during implementation.

Who uses the portal in a Canadian NDT company

Level III and QA managers

They write or approve course content, set quiz pass marks, decide which courses each crew needs for each client, and use completion records when an owner's quality management system audit or a nuclear operator's contractor review comes around.

Radiation safety officers

They assign radiation safety and source transport content, check that every operator, assistant and driver has completed it, and keep that evidence ready for a CNSC inspection.

Technicians and trainees

They see their courses on the dashboard, study between rotations, take quizzes and open Practical NDT when they want practice. A trainee waiting to sit a CGSB exam can keep building familiarity with a method in the meantime, even though the portal itself isn't exam preparation.

Operations and dispatch

They see training alongside certification status and availability, so a technician isn't sent to an oil sands site or a nuclear outage without the client's required course completed.

HR and admin

They create learner accounts for new hires and turnaround staff, and revoke access when people leave or a contract ends. That keeps client procedures and company material inside the company.

Frequently asked questions

Does the portal prepare technicians for CGSB exams?

No. It is for your company's internal training: onboarding, procedures, client requirements, safety and refreshers. Atlantis's own courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A.

Can the ERP record CGSB certifications?

Yes. The Certificates app records ISO 9712-based certifications, including CGSB, alongside SNT-TC-1A and others, with expiry tracking.

Can it deliver our CNSC or TDG training?

It can deliver and record company content your RSO chooses. Whether that meets your licence and TDG obligations is your RSO's decision.

Does it work in French?

You can build French versions of courses and assign learners to the right language.

Can crews study from camp?

Yes, with a working internet connection, since lessons stream from OneDrive or SharePoint.

What does it cost?

Quote on request, based on scope and customization.
